note: Featured blog posts rotated weekly on the dashboard 'Story of the week' card. Ordered newest-ish first; rotation is deterministic by ISO week so it changes without a deploy. Edit freely.

stories.title: We Fact-Checked Our Own Site — and Changed 33 Numbers
stories.blurb: We turned our own scrutiny on ourselves: a site-wide audit of every statistic against current primary sources. Here's what was wrong, and how we now check every week.

stories.title: The Pollution You Can't See Being Emitted
stories.blurb: Up to 42% of India's PM2.5 isn't emitted directly — it forms in the sky from gases like SO₂. Dust-first clean-air spending misses most of it.

stories.title: NCAP at the Finish Line: Has It Worked?
stories.blurb: The National Clean Air Programme's deadline has elapsed. We follow the promises and the money to see which cities delivered — and which moved backwards.

stories.title: The $339 Billion Question: What Pollution Costs India
stories.blurb: Dirty air isn't only a health story — it's an economic one. Lost workdays, lower yields, and a bill worth about 9.5% of GDP.

stories.title: India's Children Are Paying the Price
stories.blurb: Smaller lungs, higher exposure, developing brains. Why children carry a disproportionate share of the air-pollution burden.

stories.title: How Farmers Outsmart Satellites: The Stubble-Burning Shell Game
stories.blurb: Fire counts fell — but so did the satellites' ability to see them. A look at what the overpass-timing shift hides.

stories.title: A City Is Not One Number: Mapping India's Air Ward by Ward
stories.blurb: Your city's headline AQI hides enormous variation. We map fine-particle pollution down to the municipal ward.

stories.title: The Lancet's Causal Evidence: 1.5 Million Deaths
stories.blurb: Correlation isn't causation — until it is. How Jaganathan et al. 2024 established a causal link between PM2.5 and mortality in India.
